egress.terms: Free. Files come from Kaggle's Google-hosted CDN (storage.googleapis.com) with no egress meter. Downloads require a Kaggle API token.

tooling: kagglehub and the Kaggle API. Endpoints GET /api/v1/models/list and GET /api/v1/models/google/bert/get return HTTP 200 with model records. Datasets endpoint /api/v1/datasets/list returns JSON with totalBytesNullable per dataset. Model uploading via API is restricted to designated accounts, and kagglehub limits repositories to 50 files before creating archives.
chaining: Models and datasets are separate quota pools, so the ceiling is 200 GB private models + 200 GB private datasets + 200 GB per public model × N public models + 200 GB per public dataset × N public datasets. Public items are the real multiplier. Each model can carry multiple variations and frameworks, but they share the model's 200 GB.

limits_note: Per-object-cap 200 GB and 50 top-level files per dataset. 'A max of 50 top-level files (if you have more, use a directory structure and upload an archive)'. Uploading via the API is write-gated for most accounts. Practical caveat from the docs: archives are uncompressed server-side so their contents are usable in Notebooks, which means the 200 GB is measured on the expanded tree.
reliability_note: Kaggle is Google-owned and long-lived; the risk is policy drift on public storage, not disappearance. The 200 GB private pool is enforced hard ('if you exceed this, either make your datasets public or delete unused datasets').

extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
